newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Trelleborg says Boliden in Mexico joint venture.
newsitem.headline: Trelleborg says Boliden in Mexico joint venture.

text.p: Swedish mining and rubber group Trelleborg said on Wednesday that its metals unit Boliden had joined forces with Canada's Silver Eagle Resources Ltd in a new prospecting company in Mexico.
Boliden and Silver Eagle will start prospecting for base and precious metals within a concession called Minera Serrana, which is owned by Silver Eagle, Trelleborg said in a statement.
The area is in Sonora, northern Mexico, and is more than 2,300 square kms with already identified findings of zinc, led and silver.
A second phase for the prospecting aims to identify zinc, gold and copper findings in other parts of Mexico.

After the first phase, Boliden will hold 51 percent of the concession in Minera Serrana. In the second phase, Boliden will own 51 percent of all base metal projects, while the remaining 49 percent will be held by Silver Eagle.
Boliden will have operative responsibility for these projects, while Silver Eagle will be responsbile for precious metal projects of which it will hold 51 percent and Boliden 49 percent.
"We continue to focus on middle and South America," Boliden's chief executive Anders Bulow said.
"We have previously signed an agreement with Oro Belle about prospecting in Argentina.

"Our deal with Silver Eagle opens many opportunities for us in Mexico, a country that is very interesting from a mining point of view as the ore is of a kind that Boliden has a lot of experience with."
